description: One extractor feeds a barracks through a five-cell conduit; buffers drained each tick.
A splitter alternates between a direct barracks and a barracks two cells away; drained.
Two sources of the same resource join in a merger feeding a turret; drained.

A merger fed directly by another merger (and so by an extractor) and, through a 5-cell conduit, by a second extractor, behind a barracks that takes one unit per 25 ticks: both inputs are always backed up and the merger alternates between them (each branch gets 60 of the 120 items consumed, give or take the items in flight) instead of always taking the conduit.
A crossover carries two resources through each other to a turret and an overclocker; drained.
A splitter with no output conduit: every item is lost.
Buffers are never drained: the buffer fills, the conduit fills, the source stalls, nothing is lost.

A merger fed directly by two extractors (no conduits), behind a barracks that takes one unit per 25 ticks: both sources are always ready, so the merger's round-robin pointer, not the building ID, decides who fills the cell and the two extractors alternate (each ends with about half of the items produced) instead of the lower ID monopolising it.

A merger fed directly by one extractor and, through a 5-cell conduit, by a second one, behind a barracks that takes one unit per 25 ticks: the direct source counts as ready when it would produce this tick, so the merger alternates between it and the conduit instead of always taking the conduit.

Drained: a slow direct extractor (tier 1, one item per 20 ticks) and a fast one (tier 3, one per 10 ticks) behind a 10-cell conduit feed a merger. On the tick the conduit's item reaches its last cell, the direct extractor has a countdown of 1 and would produce: it counts as ready, so the merger's round-robin pointer (which favours the direct input) lets it fill the cell and the conduit item waits one tick. If a source were ready only at countdown 0, the conduit would win that tick and the slow extractor would lose a tick (19 items instead of 20).
A tier 1 collector (50 per 1000 ticks) feeds a splitter with two tier 1 barracks (each needs 50): both are under-supplied and get an even split (PP-7).

Two tier 2 collectors (142 per 1000 ticks) feed a merger and a splitter with a tier 1 barracks (needs 50) and a tier 3 barracks (needs 100). The even share (71) is above the tier 1 barracks' top speed: its production interval, not its store, makes that path back up, and the tier 3 barracks takes the remainder.
A tier 3 and a tier 2 collector (171 per 1000 ticks) into two tier 1 barracks (50 each): both reach their top speed, both paths back up and the collectors stall; nothing is lost.
A three-way splitter with the east output unconnected: the two connected tier 1 barracks (north, west) share the items evenly; the unconnected output is skipped, nothing is lost.
Resources cross a border through a link of 15 cells; nothing is lost.
A link carries from the higher plot to the lower one.
A splitter shares evenly between the owner own barracks and a link to the neighbour barracks.
A collector feeds a splitter whose only connected outputs are two open sending halves: the splitter holds its item, the collector stalls, nothing is lost.
A splitter with one open half and one consumer: the consumer receives every item and nothing is lost.

A tier 3 Foundry fed Ore only (a tier 3 collector at top speed) on its south side and nothing on its west side: the Ore counter fills to 5, the Ore input buffer fills, the collector stalls and the Foundry never produces. Counters in the pacer: [5, 0] (sorted by resource ID: res_a, res_b).

A tier 3 Foundry fed by a tier 3 Ore collector and a tier 3 Power collector (100 items per 1000 ticks each, equal to its need per resource): it produces at its top speed, one unit per 50 ticks, and nothing is lost.

A tier 3 Foundry (need 100 per resource per 1000 ticks) with a tier 3 Ore collector and a tier 1 Power collector (50 per 1000 ticks): production follows Power (10 per 1000 ticks, 5 per unit); the Ore counter stays full, the Ore conduit backs up and the Ore collector stalls while Power is still arriving.
A tier 1 Foundry (need 50 per resource per 1000 ticks) fed by tier 1 collectors (50 per 1000 ticks each): one unit per 100 ticks.

A tier 3 Ore collector feeds a splitter that shares Ore between a tier 3 Foundry and a tier 3 Barracks (one cost for any resource); a tier 3 Power collector feeds the Foundry directly. Ore is the scarce input: the Foundry waits for its Ore counter while the Barracks takes its half, and the Power counter stays full meanwhile.

Player 1 owns a tier 3 Foundry and a tier 3 Ore collector; its Power comes over a border link (PP-4) from a tier 3 Power collector of player 0, across 10 + 3 conduit cells. The link only delays the first Power; the Foundry then runs at its top speed.

A tier 3 Ore collector and a tier 3 Power collector feed a tier 3 Composite refinery (3 of each per batch, 30 ticks, 2 Composite per batch, 66 per 1000 ticks at top speed); its output conduit feeds a test consumer of Composite (extraBuildings; it takes one per 10 ticks, more than the refinery makes). The refinery paces itself; the consumer is paced in need mode.
The same chain for the Aether refinery: Power on its south input, Flux on its west input; the test consumer takes Aether.
A tier 1 Composite refinery (60 ticks per batch, 33 per 1000 ticks) fed by two tier 3 collectors: the collectors back up (the refinery takes 3 of each per 60 ticks), nothing is lost.
Composite refinery with Ore but no Power: the Ore counter fills to 3 and the Ore buffer and conduit back up; the refinery never makes a batch and nothing reaches the consumer.

The refined conduit ends at a test consumer that nothing paces (hold mode): its buffer fills, the conduit fills, the refinery's output store holds an item and the refinery is stalled; intake stops (counters and input buffers full) and both collectors stall.
A Composite refinery whose output has no conduit: every item is sent into nothing and counts as lost (hold mode); batches continue at the top speed.
A test consumer of Composite sits directly against the refinery's north side (a conduit of length 0): items pass on the tick they leave the store.
The Composite chain in drain mode: the consumer's buffer is emptied every tick; the refinery's own buffers are not drained and it works as in the other modes.

Player 1's tier 3 Aether refinery gets Power from its own collector and Flux over a border link from player 0 (PP-4); its output conduit feeds a test consumer of Aether. The refined item is the same resource type whichever player owns the chain.

Two tier 2 Ore collectors feed a tier 2 Grand barracks (3x3, 4 Ore per soldier, two soldiers per production, 8 items per production every 56 ticks) through a Merger: the dry run in need mode shows both collectors fully feeding it (need 142 per 1000 ticks, no source stalls).

One tier 2 Ore collector feeds a tier 2 Grand barracks through a Merger: it fills its 8-item production at half the speed of two collectors (about half the productions of grand-barracks-two-collectors-need) and the collector never stalls.
The tunnel-under-walls layout run for 1000 ticks with the consumers paced at their need: the Barracks is fed through the pair as through a conduit (CB-9g), no item is lost.

Transit time of a Tunnel pair (CB-9g): an Ore collector, 2 conduit cells, a Tunnel pair of distance 4 (ends at y 5 and 9) and a Barracks directly north of the exit, run for 25 ticks. The first Ore item has not arrived yet: the same line built with Mergers at the two end cells and a conduit of the 3 cells between them (flow-sim.tunnel-transit-conduit) delivers its first item one tick earlier, in the last of the 25 ticks. A tunnel is never faster than a conduit.

The comparison for flow-sim.tunnel-transit-pair: Mergers at the same two cells joined by a conduit of the 3 cells between them. The first Ore item arrives one tick earlier than through the Tunnel pair, so after the same 25 ticks one item is delivered.

The Mana Well makes half what an Extractor of its tier does (issue #473): over 400 ticks a tier 1 Extractor on a node makes an item every 20 ticks, a tier 1 Well every 40 (feeding a Barracks with Ore), a tier 2 Well every 28 (Power into a Hangar) and a tier 3 Well every 20 (Flux, unconnected, so its items are lost).

The same board as mana-well-rate, after the owner changed two settings between battles (issue #473): the tier 2 Well (id 4) is now Ore and the tier 1 Well (id 2) now Power, so both conduits were detached; their items are lost and the Barracks and the Hangar get nothing.
